rulings.ruling: Ruling: project retained (owner, T-043; amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property). The second follows Worksheet 1 (i4562 p. 4), whose line 3 takes the smaller of the cost of 2025 property and $2,500,000. The project follows the line 1 instruction on the same page ('Generally, the maximum section 179 expense deduction is $2,500,000'), for which the worksheet is offered as an optional aid ('You can use Worksheet 1'). Research from the archived 26 U.S.C. 179(b)(3)(B) and Treas. Reg. 1.179-3(b)-(c) (ambiguities/research/amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property.md) shows the two agree on every return without a carryover, because an election never exceeds the cost, and that on a return with one the worksheet's cap departs from the statute, which measures a carryover against the dollar limitation.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 12 is never more than lines 9 and 10 ('Add lines 9 and 10, but don't enter more than line 11'), so lines 9 + 10 - 12 is never negative and the project's floor at zero changes nothing.

Ruling: second transcription right in substance, resolved by refusal (owner, BUG-0062). On a separate return line 2 includes the spouse's section 179 property (i4562 p. 4, Line 2) and the line 5 limitation is shared (p. 5); the project now refuses a section 179 election or carryover on a separate return (s179.mfs, on line 5). On every other return line 2 is the same sum on both sides.

Ruling: second transcription right in substance, resolved by refusal (owner, BUG-0062). On a separate return line 2 includes the spouse's section 179 property (i4562 p. 4, Line 2) and the line 5 limitation is shared (p. 5); the project refuses a section 179 election or carryover on a separate return (s179.mfs, on line 5), so no deduction can differ. On a separate return with neither, line 2 omits the spouse's property; lines 4 and 5 then print differently only if the couple's 2025 section 179 property costs more than $4,000,000, and line 12 is zero either way. On every other return line 2 is the same sum on both sides.

Ruling: second transcription right in substance, resolved by refusal (owner, BUG-0062). The second halves line 5 on a separate return and refuses an unequal allocation (i4562 p. 5, Line 5); the project refuses any section 179 election or carryover on a separate return (s179.mfs). Otherwise both subtract line 4 from line 1, floored at zero.
